## Import & Set-up

Libraries

```{r echo=T, error=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results='hide'}
library(tidyverse)
library(lme4)
library(buildmer)
library(afex)
library(boot)
library(cowplot)
set.seed(123)
```

Reading in data & excluding observations

```{r}
reptext_long <- read.csv("repetition_texting_tm_data.csv")
reptext_long <- subset(reptext_long, exclude_obs == FALSE)
```

## Pre-registered analyses

### H1: Truth-ratings

Pre-registration:

> Truth Ratings: We will analyze these data using a mixed-effects linear regression model with truth ratings as the DV, views as the IV, and random effects by participant and headline. We will use the 'buildmer' package in R to select the model with the maximal random effects structure that will still converge, using the 'bobyqa' optimizer, the 'order' direction parameter, and the 'LRT' criterion. To test if the effect of multiple repetitions is linear or logarithmic, we will compare models with the raw number of views as a predictor vs. the natural logarithm of the number of views, both of which will have random effects structures determined by the process described above. H1 predicts that belief will increase as a function of repetition, and that the model using the natural log of the number of views as a predictor will produce a better fit to the data.


Isolating truth ratings

```{r}
reptext_long_truth <- subset(reptext_long, rating_type == "Tru")
```

#### Model 1: Truth ratings as a function of repetition

```{r message=FALSE}
truthmodel1.max <- rating ~ 1 + repetition + (1+repetition|claim) + (1+repetition|subjId)

truthmodel1.build <- buildmer(truthmodel1.max,data=reptext_long_truth,buildmerControl=buildmerControl(direction='order',args=list(control=lmerControl(optimizer='bobyqa'))))
truthmodel1.formula <- formula(truthmodel1.build@model)
truthmodel1.final <- lmer(truthmodel1.formula,reptext_long_truth, control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa"))

print(truthmodel1.formula)
summary(truthmodel1.final)
```

#### Model 2: Truth ratings as a function of the log of repetition

```{r message=FALSE}
truthmodel2.max <- rating ~ 1 + repetitionlog + (1+repetitionlog|claim)+(1+repetitionlog|subjId )

truthmodel2.build <- buildmer(truthmodel2.max,data=reptext_long_truth,buildmerControl=buildmerControl(direction='order',args=list(control=lmerControl(optimizer='bobyqa'))))
truthmodel2.formula <- formula(truthmodel2.build@model)
truthmodel2.final <- lmer(truthmodel2.formula,reptext_long_truth, control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa"))

print(truthmodel2.formula)
summary(truthmodel2.final)
```

#### Model comparison

```{r}
anova(truthmodel1.final,truthmodel2.final, test = "Chisq")
```

### H2a-d: Unethicality ratings

Isolating ethicality ratings

```{r}
reptext_long_eth <- subset(reptext_long, rating_type == "Eth")
```


#### H2a: Unethicality ratings as a function of exposure

Pre-registration:

> Ethicality ratings: We will analyze these data using a mixed-effects linear regression model with unethicality ratings as the DV, repetition (1 = seen at least once previously, 0 = not previously seen) as the IV, and random effects by participant and headline. We will determine the random effects structure using 'buildmer' as described above. H2a predicts that headlines seen at least once before will be rated as less unethical than novel headlines (i.e., a negative coefficient for the IV).

```{r message=FALSE}
#getting descriptives
meansbyexp <- reptext_long_eth %>% 
  group_by(exposure) %>% 
  summarise(mean=mean(rating), se=sd(rating)/(sqrt(n())),
            CI_low=mean-(1.96*se), CI_high=mean+(1.96*se))

meansbyexp


#running model
h2a_model.max <- rating ~ 1 + exposure + (1+exposure|claim)+(1+exposure|subjId )

h2a_model.build <- buildmer(h2a_model.max,data=reptext_long_eth,buildmerControl=buildmerControl(direction='order',args=list(control=lmerControl(optimizer='bobyqa'))))
h2a_model.formula <- formula(h2a_model.build@model)
h2a_model.build.final <- lmer(h2a_model.formula,reptext_long_eth, control=lmerControl(optimizer='bobyqa'))

print(h2a_model.formula)
summary(h2a_model.build.final)
```

#### H2b: Mediation analysis from exposure to unethicality ratings with anger and norm perception as parallel mediators

Pre-registration:

> Next, to test H2b, we will compute a multilevel mediation model from exposure (seen at least once vs. not previously seen) to anger and norm perception as parallel mediators, to unethicality ratings. The model will have the same random effect structure used in testing H2a. H2b predicts a significant indirect effect with a negative coefficient through anger, such that prior exposure to a headline reduces how angry it makes people feel, and that reduced anger predicts lower unethicality ratings. We are also interested in exploring mediation through norm perceptions (i.e., whether prior exposure makes wrongdoing seem less unusual, which in turn reduces how unethical it seems), but we are not formalizing a hypothesis about this possibility.

Using approach suggested by Bauer, Preacher & Gil (2006), as demonstrated here: <https://stats.idre.ucla.edu/r/faq/how-can-i-perform-mediation-with-multilevel-data-method-2/>


```{r}
#creating stacked format data for mediation model
reptext_long_morality <- subset(reptext_long, rating_type != "Tru")

reptext_wide_morality <- reptext_long_morality %>% 
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = c(subjId,claim,exposure,repetitionlog),
    names_from = rating_type,
    values_from = rating
  )

reptext_stack_morality <- reptext_wide_morality %>% 
  #duplicating measures to stack
  mutate(
    Ang_pivot = Ang,
    Nor_pivot = Nor,
    Eth_pivot = Eth
  ) %>% 
  #pivoting by duplicated measures to create stacked dataframe
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Ang_pivot, Nor_pivot, Eth_pivot),
    names_to = "measure"
  ) %>% 
  #removing "_pivot" suffix, then adding selection variables for model
  mutate(
    measure = substr(measure,1,3),
    select_Ang = as.integer(measure == "Ang"),
    select_Nor = as.integer(measure == "Nor"),
    select_Eth = as.integer(measure == "Eth")
  )

#preview of what the data look like
head(reptext_stack_morality)
```

Now, for the full model.

```{r}
h2b_mediation <- lmer(value ~ 0 + 
                        select_Ang + select_Ang:exposure +
                        select_Nor + select_Nor:exposure +
                        select_Eth + select_Eth:exposure + select_Eth:Ang + select_Eth:Nor + 
                        (0 + select_Eth + select_Eth:exposure| subjId) +
                        (0 + select_Eth + select_Eth:exposure| claim),
                      data = reptext_stack_morality
                        )

summary(h2b_mediation)
vcov(h2b_mediation)
fixef(h2b_mediation)
VarCorr(h2b_mediation)
```


Bootstrapped confidence intervals for indirect effect via anger

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, cache = TRUE}
h2b_ang_ie = function(formula, data, random) {
  d = data[random, ]
  model = lmer(formula, data = d)
  a = fixef(model)[4]
  b = fixef(model)[7]
  indirect = as.numeric(a*b)
  return(indirect)
}


h2b_ang_boot = boot(data = reptext_stack_morality,
                   statistic = h2b_ang_ie,
                   formula = value ~ 0 + 
                        select_Ang + select_Ang:exposure +
                        select_Nor + select_Nor:exposure +
                        select_Eth + select_Eth:exposure + select_Eth:Ang + select_Eth:Nor + 
                        (0 + select_Eth + select_Eth:exposure| subjId) +
                        (0 + select_Eth + select_Eth:exposure| claim),
                   R = 2000)

h2b_ang_boot
boot.ci(h2b_ang_boot,
        conf = .95,
        type = "norm")
```


Bootstrapped confidence intervals for indirect effect via norm perception

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, cache = TRUE}
h2b_nor_ie = function(formula, data, random) {
  d = data[random, ]
  model = lmer(formula, data = d)
  a = fixef(model)[5]
  b = fixef(model)[8]
  indirect = as.numeric(a*b)
  return(indirect)
}


h2b_nor_boot = boot(data = reptext_stack_morality,
                   statistic = h2b_nor_ie,
                   formula = value ~ 0 + 
                        select_Ang + select_Ang:exposure +
                        select_Nor + select_Nor:exposure +
                        select_Eth + select_Eth:exposure + select_Eth:Ang + select_Eth:Nor + 
                        (0 + select_Eth + select_Eth:exposure| subjId) +
                        (0 + select_Eth + select_Eth:exposure| claim),
                   R = 2000)

h2b_nor_boot
boot.ci(h2b_nor_boot,
        conf = .95,
        type = "norm")
```

#### H2c: Unethicality ratings as a function of quantity of repetitions (H2c)

Pre-registration:

> To test H2c, we will follow the same analysis plan that tested H1, except the DV will be unethicality ratings. H2c predicts that the negative effect of number of repetitions on unethicality ratings will get smaller as the number of repetitions increases. That is, we expect that unethicality judgments will decrease as a function of the number of views, and that the model with the natural log of the number of views will fit the data better than the model with the linear effect of the number of views.

##### Model 1: Unethicality ratings as a function of repetition

```{r message=FALSE}
ethmodel1.max <- rating ~ 1 + repetition + (1+repetition|claim)+(1+repetition|subjId )

ethmodel1.build <- buildmer(ethmodel1.max,data=reptext_long_eth,buildmerControl=buildmerControl(direction='order',args=list(control=lmerControl(optimizer='bobyqa'))))
ethmodel1.formula <- formula(ethmodel1.build@model)
ethmodel1.final <- lmer(ethmodel1.formula,reptext_long_eth,control=lmerControl(optimizer='bobyqa'))

print(ethmodel1.formula)
summary(ethmodel1.final)
```

##### Model 2: Unethicality ratings as a function of the log of repetition

```{r message=FALSE}
ethmodel2.max <- rating ~ 1 + repetitionlog + (1+repetitionlog|claim)+(1+repetitionlog|subjId )

ethmodel2.build <- buildmer(ethmodel2.max,data=reptext_long_eth,buildmerControl=buildmerControl(direction='order',args=list(control=lmerControl(optimizer='bobyqa'))))
ethmodel2.formula <- formula(ethmodel2.build@model)
ethmodel2.final <- lmer(ethmodel2.formula,reptext_long_eth,control=lmerControl(optimizer='bobyqa'))

print(ethmodel2.formula)
summary(ethmodel2.final)
```

##### Model comparison

```{r}
anova(ethmodel1.final,ethmodel2.final)
```

#### H2d: Mediation analysis from repettion to unethicality ratings with anger and norm perception as mediators

Pre-registration:

>Finally, we will compute a multilevel mediation analysis to test whether this logarithmic effect is mediated by anger above and beyond norm perception (H2d). The model will have the same random effect structure used in testing H2c.

```{r}
h2d_mediation <- lmer(value ~ 0 + 
                        select_Ang + select_Ang:repetitionlog +
                        select_Nor + select_Nor:repetitionlog +
                        select_Eth + select_Eth:repetitionlog + select_Eth:Ang + select_Eth:Nor + 
                        (0 + select_Eth + select_Eth:repetitionlog| subjId) +
                        (0 + select_Eth + select_Eth:repetitionlog| claim),
                      data = reptext_stack_morality
                        )

summary(h2d_mediation)
vcov(h2d_mediation)
fixef(h2d_mediation)
VarCorr(h2d_mediation)
```



Bootstrapped confidence intervals for indirect effect via anger

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, cache = TRUE}

h2d_ang_boot = boot(data = reptext_stack_morality,
                   statistic = h2d_ang_ie,

```

## Other analyses

### Exploratory mediation model

Ccreating stacked format data for mediation model, with truth, anger & norm perception measures

```{r}
reptext_wide_exp <- reptext_long %>% 
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = c(subjId,claim,exposure,repetitionlog),
    names_from = rating_type,
    values_from = rating
  )

reptext_stack_exp <- reptext_wide_exp %>% 
  #duplicating measures to stack
  mutate(
    Ang_pivot = Ang,
    Nor_pivot = Nor,
    Eth_pivot = Eth,
    Tru_pivot = Tru,
  ) %>% 
  #pivoting by duplicated measures to create stacked dataframe
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Ang_pivot, Nor_pivot, Eth_pivot, Tru_pivot),
    names_to = "measure"
  ) %>% 
  #removing "_pivot" suffix, then adding selection variables for model
  mutate(
    measure = substr(measure,1,3),
    select_Ang = as.integer(measure == "Ang"),
    select_Nor = as.integer(measure == "Nor"),
    select_Eth = as.integer(measure == "Eth"),
    select_Tru = as.integer(measure == "Tru")
  )

#preview of what the data look like
head(reptext_stack_exp)
```


```{r}
exp_mediation <- lmer(value ~ 0 + 
                        select_Ang + select_Ang:exposure +
                        select_Nor + select_Nor:exposure +
                        select_Tru + select_Tru:exposure +
                        select_Eth + select_Eth:exposure + 
                        select_Eth:Ang + select_Eth:Nor + select_Eth:Tru +
                        (0 + select_Eth + select_Eth:exposure| subjId) +
                        (0 + select_Eth + select_Eth:exposure| claim),
                      data = reptext_stack_exp
                        )
summary(exp_mediation)
vcov(exp_mediation)
fixef(exp_mediation)
VarCorr(exp_mediation)
```

bootstrapped confidence intervals for the indirect effect through truth

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, cache=TRUE}
exp_tru_ie = function(formula, data, random) {
  d = data[random, ]
  model = lmer(formula, data = d)
  a = fixef(model)[7]
  b = fixef(model)[11]
  indirect = as.numeric(a*b)
  return(indirect)
}

exp_tru_boot = boot(data = reptext_stack_exp,
                   statistic = exp_tru_ie,
                   formula = value ~ 0 + 
                        select_Ang + select_Ang:exposure +
                        select_Nor + select_Nor:exposure +
                        select_Tru + select_Tru:exposure +
                        select_Eth + select_Eth:exposure + 
                        select_Eth:Ang + select_Eth:Nor + select_Eth:Tru +
                        (0 + select_Eth + select_Eth:exposure| subjId) +
                        (0 + select_Eth + select_Eth:exposure| claim),
                   R = 2000)

exp_tru_boot
boot.ci(exp_tru_boot,
        conf = .95,
        type = "norm")
```

### Number of participants detecting hypothesis

Summarizing number of responses to the open-ended question about participants' perception of the study's intent as a) referencing a link between unethicality and repetition and b) referencing desensitization or changes in feelings with exposure.

```{r}
reptext_long %>% 
  group_by(subjId) %>% 
  summarise(purpose_coded_a = modeest::mlv(purpose_coded_a), purpose_coded_b  = modeest::mlv(purpose_coded_b)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  summarise(purpose_coded_a = sum(purpose_coded_a), purpose_coded_b  = sum(purpose_coded_b))
```


### Exploratory model comparison

Comparing a model predicting unethicality ratings from repetition (h2a_model.build.final) and from the natural logarithm of the number of views (ethmodel2.final)

```{r}
anova(h2a_model.build.final,ethmodel2.final)
```

### Cohens dz

Effect of repetition on morality

```{r}
reptext_wide_morality_dz <- reptext_long %>% 
  filter(rating_type == "Eth") %>% 
  group_by(subjId, exposure) %>% 
  summarise(Eth = mean(rating)) %>% 
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = subjId,
    names_from = exposure,
    names_prefix = "exp",
    values_from = Eth
  )

#ethicality
eth_md <- mean(reptext_wide_morality_dz$exp1) - mean(reptext_wide_morality_dz$exp0)
eth_sd <- sd(reptext_wide_morality_dz$exp1 - reptext_wide_morality_dz$exp0)

eth_dz <- eth_md/eth_sd
eth_dz
```

Effect of repetition on truth

```{r}
reptext_wide_truth_dz <- reptext_long %>% 
  filter(rating_type == "Tru") %>% 
  group_by(subjId, exposure) %>% 
  summarise(Tru = mean(rating)) %>% 
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = subjId,
    names_from = exposure,
    names_prefix = "exp",
    values_from = Tru
  )

#ethicality
tru_md <- mean(reptext_wide_truth_dz$exp1) - mean(reptext_wide_truth_dz$exp0)
tru_sd <- sd(reptext_wide_truth_dz$exp1 - reptext_wide_truth_dz$exp0)

tru_dz <- tru_md/tru_sd
tru_dz
```
